strategy.summary: Three tests named in SYNC-21 pass and fail on the same commit. A probe (10 shuffled runs) confirmed each is flaky. retry: the test waits a fixed 40ms, but the back-off is 20–59ms because of random jitter. subscribers: the handler registry is shared by the whole process, and another test in the same file leaves its handlers subscribed, so the outcome depends on the shuffled order CI uses. saveAll: src/bulk.js pushes ids in the order the saves finish, not the order of the records. That is an application defect, so that test is quarantined and filed as an issue. Every existing assertion and test case is kept.
inScope: test/retry.test.js: make the back-off test deterministic
test/subscribers.test.js: isolate the tests from the process-wide handler registry
test/bulk.test.js: quarantine the saveAll ordering test, record the defect and file it as an issue
outOfScope: Changing application code (src/bulk.js), which is the application's to fix
assumptions: CI runs `npx vitest run --sequence.shuffle` (.github/workflows/ci.yml), so the tests must not depend on their order
src/bulk.js's doc comment (ids in the order of `records`) is the intended contract, so the saveAll test is right and the code is wrong

risks.description: The saveAll test stays skipped until src/bulk.js is fixed, so an ordering regression would go unnoticed meanwhile
risks.mitigation: A GitHub issue is filed with the evidence, and the skip comment names the cause so the test can be re-enabled once the code is fixed

acceptanceCriteria.text: retry › retries a failed call after a back-off passes on every run, with no fixed sleep, and still proves the call is retried after the back-off and resolves with the result
subscribers › stops telling a handler once it unsubscribes passes in any test order, and still proves an unsubscribed handler is not called

saveAll › resolves with the ids in the order of the records no longer fails CI at random. Its cause is in src/bulk.js, so the test is quarantined with its assertions kept, and the defect is recorded and filed

testCases.title: retries a failed call after a back-off
steps: Use vi fake timers (restored in afterEach)
Call retry with a task that fails once then succeeds, with random fixed to 0
Check the task was called once before the back-off has passed
Advance the fake clock by retryDelay(0) and check the task was called twice
testCases.expected: The task is called twice after the back-off, and retry resolves with 'ok'
testCases.rationale: Cause: the test sleeps a fixed 40ms with a real setTimeout, but retry waits retryDelay(0) = 20ms + floor(Math.random()*40), which is 20–59ms. When the jitter goes past about 20ms, the second call hasn't happened yet (probe: 6 of 10 runs failed with 'called 1 times'). Fixing the jitter and driving a fake clock removes the timing guess.

testCases.title: stops telling a handler once it unsubscribes
steps: Have every test in the file register the unsubscribe function each subscribe returns, and call them all in afterEach
Subscribe a handler to 'records', unsubscribe it, then publish
testCases.expected: publish returns 0 and the handler is not called, in any test order
testCases.rationale: Cause: src/subscribers.js keeps one module-level handlers Map for the whole process. 'tells every handler subscribed to the topic' subscribes two handlers to 'records' and never unsubscribes them, so when it runs first under CI's --sequence.shuffle, publish returns 2 (probe: 'expected 2 to be +0' with 5 shuffle seeds). Unsubscribing everything after each test gives each test a clean registry.

testCases.title: resolves with the ids in the order of the records
steps: Keep the test and its assertions unchanged
Quarantine it with it.skip and a comment naming the cause in src/bulk.js
Record the defect and file a GitHub issue
testCases.expected: The test is skipped until saveAll keeps the order of the records
testCases.rationale: Cause in application code: saveAll (src/bulk.js:7-10) runs the saves concurrently and pushes each id when its save resolves. The records client has random latency, so ids come back in completion order, not record order (probe: ['second','first'] in 4 of 10 runs). The test is correct. Only the app can fix this, for example by returning the Promise.all result.

strategy.environmentNotes: No services are needed. The tests are pure Vitest unit tests, run in a shuffled order as CI does.

defects.title: saveAll resolves with ids in completion order, not the order of the records
defects.description: src/bulk.js documents that saveAll resolves with the ids in the order of `records`, so callers can pair them by index. Instead, saveAll (src/bulk.js:6-12) runs every client.save concurrently and calls `ids.push(await client.save(record))` as each save finishes. The records client's latency varies (random up to latencyMs), so when a later record's save finishes first, its id comes first. Expected: ['first','second']. Actual, at random: ['second','first']. Fix: return the result of `Promise.all(records.map((r) => client.save(r)))`, which keeps the input order.
defects.evidence: probe_stability, 10 shuffled runs: 'saveAll resolves with the ids in the order of the records' passed 6 of 10. It failed 4× with "AssertionError: expected [ 'second', 'first' ] to deeply equal [ 'first', 'second' ]" at test/bulk.test.js:10. The saveEach test with the same assertion passed every run.
